ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the right side of the figure there are upper and lower output terminals. On the left side is a current source labeled 3A, with the arrow direction upward; in the middle/right side there is a resistor labeled 2Ω. The current source and the 2Ω resistor are both connected between the same pair of upper and lower nodes, so they form a parallel Norton equivalent source. Reasoning: When converting the Norton form to the Thevenin voltage source form, the equivalent voltage is V = I·R = 3A × 2Ω = 6V, and the equivalent series resistance is still 2Ω. Since the current source arrow is upward, current is injected into the upper node, so the upper end of the equivalent voltage source is positive and the lower end is negative.
